title: Benchmarking
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and behavior of benchmarking.
Apply at least one lesson concept—benchmark functions—in a small Go example or workflow.
Predict a representative result, then test a boundary case and explain any difference.

content.intro: Benchmarking is part of Go’s feedback loop for correctness and maintainability. Use a focused test or diagnostic that matches the suspected defect, keep the reproduction small, and treat passing tests as evidence for the cases exercised rather than proof that all cases are correct.
content.why_it_matters: Tests and diagnostics catch regressions early and make refactoring safer, especially as concurrency and application complexity grow.

content_blocks.title: A fast feedback loop
content_blocks.alt_text: Focused tests, static checks, race detection, and fuzzing cover different defect classes; none alone proves correctness. Labeled phases: Write assertion; Run go test; Add vet / race / fuzz; Review missing cases.

content.task: Create a small example connected to “Benchmarking”. Use Benchmark functions as the starting point, predict the output, then add one invalid, empty, or boundary case and document its result.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates benchmark functions or a closely related concept.
Inputs, relevant state changes, and expected output are clear.
At least one boundary case is deliberately tested or documented.
Errors are handled honestly and no success state is reported when the operation fails.
hints: Start from the simplest example related to benchmark functions.
Predict the result manually and annotate the value that changes at each step.
Run `gofmt` and the appropriate local `go run`, `go test`, `go vet`, or inspection command when prerequisites are available.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the happy-path output proves all inputs are safe.
common_mistakes.why: Empty, malformed, boundary, or concurrent cases may follow different paths.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused tests for a normal input and at least one relevant edge case.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring returned errors or external-system status.
common_mistakes.why: Go APIs commonly report expected failures as explicit error values.
common_mistakes.fix: Check errors close to the operation, add useful context when propagating, and clean up resources.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an API or syntax without checking the selected Go version.
common_mistakes.why: Language and standard-library capabilities can change between releases.
common_mistakes.fix: Record `go version`, inspect the `go` directive, and read official release notes for version-specific topics.

summary: Benchmarking provides a reusable rule or workflow for Go programs.
The subtopics to revisit are: Benchmark functions; Measuring operations per second; Comparing implementations; Controlling benchmark variables; Identifying unreliable benchmark results.
Prefer a small reproducible example, explicit errors, appropriate tests, and version-matched official documentation.
